title: Region-aware SLO contracts, circuit-breaker telemetry, and token-shed heatmap
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: create a set of measurable SLO contracts and dashboards that make region-aware failover and circuit-breaker behavior observable at token granularity. This ticket covers: (1) authoring SLO contracts that incorporate region-level burn rates and cross-region fallbacks, (2) adding telemetry for circuit-breaker state transitions and reasons, and (3) building a token-shed heatmap visualization to surface where load-shedding or KV-cache cold starts are causing tail latency. Goal: reduce undetected multi-region regression windows and shorten RTT to recovery when an overloaded region triggers breakers or starts shedding tokens.
acceptance_criteria: SLO contract document checked into Confluence with region-level targets and error budget allocation rules
New metrics emitted: request.sli.token_latency_ms_by_position, request.sli.kv_cache_hit_rate, circuitbreaker.state_transitions, circuitbreaker.trigger_reason
Dashboards: region SLO burn-rate view + circuit-breaker timeline + token-shed heatmap for top 10 routes/models
Alerts: burn-rate alert that triggers ops runbook and automated mild-throttling policy
Integration tests that validate metric tags and a simulated region failover produce expected dashboard state
implementation_notes: Emit token-level latency histogram with 'position' tag (position=0..N) and 'route' and 'model' tags; avoid high-cardinality tags where possible
Circuit-breaker events should include reason tags: 'queue_depth', 'token_backpressure', 'kv_cold_miss', 'kernel_timeout'
Heatmap buckets = position (0-7, 8-31, 32-127, 128+) to limit cardinality while preserving tail patterns
Backend: use metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Mimir/Thanos) for counters and a streaming aggregator to precompute heatmap grid for Grafana
Dashboard panels: (a) region SLO burn by day and rolling 6h, (b) circuit-breaker timeline heatmap, (c) top routes by token-shed ratio
Add synthetic test that injects delayed responses in a single region to validate circuit-breaker triggers and SLO burn attribution
